stem: A records schedule normally deletes customer correspondence after three years. Legal counsel issues a preservation notice covering a defined group of customers because litigation is reasonably anticipated. An automated deletion job is scheduled to remove some covered records that night. What is the BEST records-lifecycle action?
decision_point: suspend normal disposition for records within an authorized legal hold while preserving scope, integrity, and eventual controlled release
misconceptions: normal retention always overrides legal hold
all records must be kept forever after any dispute
backups alone satisfy preservation without controlling deletion

originality.authoring_note: Sibling of the released archive-migration item, but this scenario tests a legal preservation hold interrupting routine disposition rather than long-term platform support.

options: Let the deletion job run because the published retention schedule can never be suspended

Pause disposition for records within the authorized hold, preserve them with appropriate integrity and access controls, document the hold scope and custodians, and resume normal disposition only after authorized release
Disable deletion for every organizational record permanently because one legal hold applies to all information
Copy the records to an unmanaged folder and allow the normal system to delete them without tracking the preservation action
explanation: A legal or other authorized preservation hold can supersede routine disposition for in-scope records. The hold should be scoped, documented, protected, and later released through a controlled process.
distractor_rationales: Routine schedules must accommodate applicable legal preservation requirements and authorized holds.

A legal or other authorized preservation hold can supersede routine disposition for in-scope records. The hold should be scoped, documented, protected, and later released through a controlled process.
A scoped hold does not justify indefinite retention of unrelated information and can conflict with minimization and retention obligations.
Unmanaged copying can break accountability, integrity, security, and defensible preservation evidence.

stem: A product team releases every two weeks using DevOps automation, but security review occurs only in a manual meeting immediately before production. Repeated design and dependency issues are discovered at that late gate, creating emergency waivers and release delays. Which SDLC improvement BEST addresses the pattern?
decision_point: integrate security requirements, design analysis, automated testing, and risk decisions into the delivery lifecycle rather than relying on a final manual gate
misconceptions: faster delivery requires removing security review
one final gate is the most efficient control
security belongs only to a separate security team

originality.authoring_note: Original lifecycle-integration scenario focused on moving security evidence and decisions into iterative delivery rather than adding another release gate.

options: Add a second manual security meeting on release day so more late findings can be reviewed

Integrate security requirements and threat/design review early, automate appropriate code/dependency/configuration testing in CI/CD, involve security within the product workflow, and retain explicit risk decisions for exceptions
Remove security review entirely because DevOps prioritizes release speed
Freeze all releases into an annual waterfall cycle because iterative delivery cannot support security assurance
explanation: DevSecOps integrates security practices and feedback throughout planning, design, implementation, testing, release, and operations so defects and risk decisions are addressed earlier and continuously rather than concentrated at a final gate.
distractor_rationales: Another late meeting preserves the same feedback delay that creates emergency waivers and rework.

DevSecOps integrates security practices and feedback throughout planning, design, implementation, testing, release, and operations so defects and risk decisions are addressed earlier and continuously rather than concentrated at a final gate.
Fast delivery does not require abandoning security; automation and integrated practices can improve both speed and assurance.
Waterfall can be appropriate in some contexts, but the problem is late security feedback, not the mere existence of iterative delivery.

stem: A company must provide confidential design documents to external reviewers who are allowed to read them for 30 days but must not forward, print, or continue opening them after the engagement. The files may be downloaded to managed partner devices, so network DLP alone cannot enforce the full requirement after delivery. Which control MOST directly addresses the continuing usage restrictions?
decision_point: use rights-management controls when authorization restrictions must persist with a document after distribution
misconceptions: DLP alone controls every action after download
classification labels by themselves enforce usage rights

originality.authoring_note: Sibling of the released SaaS DLP/CASB item, but this scenario tests persistent post-delivery usage restrictions where DRM is the direct control.

options: Use only TLS during download because transport encryption controls whether the recipient can print or reopen the file later

Apply an appropriate digital-rights-management or information-protection mechanism that binds access to authorized identities/devices and can enforce expiration and permitted actions, alongside the normal classification and sharing controls
Rely only on the confidentiality label printed on the first page because labels automatically prevent copying
Disable all network DLP because rights management makes upstream data controls unnecessary
explanation: DRM or equivalent information-protection controls are suited to persistent usage restrictions such as access expiration, printing limits, and identity-bound opening after a document leaves the original network boundary.
distractor_rationales: TLS protects the transfer channel but does not control what an authorized recipient can do with a downloaded document afterward.

DRM or equivalent information-protection controls are suited to persistent usage restrictions such as access expiration, printing limits, and identity-bound opening after a document leaves the original network boundary.
Labels communicate handling requirements but do not necessarily enforce technical usage restrictions by themselves.
Persistent rights controls complement rather than automatically replace DLP, classification, and other upstream safeguards.

stem: Developers use an AI coding assistant that can generate large patches across multiple repositories. The current process allows a developer to accept a generated patch, squash it into one commit, and merge after functional tests, but the organization retains no record of the generated diff before editing, security-sensitive areas touched, reviewer rationale, or additional risk testing. What is the BEST software-security improvement?
decision_point: retain accountable change provenance and require risk-based human review/testing for AI-assisted code rather than treating generated changes as inherently trusted or inherently prohibited
misconceptions: AI-generated code needs no review if tests pass
all AI coding should be banned regardless of controls
squashing changes should erase provenance requirements

originality.authoring_note: Original AI-assisted software-change scenario focused on auditable provenance, accountable human review, and risk-based verification rather than configuration-image provenance.

options: Treat AI-generated patches as trusted if functional tests pass because the assistant is part of the approved development environment
Ban all AI-assisted coding permanently because generated software can never be reviewed safely

Require traceable change records and accountable human review, identify security-sensitive modifications, run appropriate static/dynamic/dependency and targeted security tests based on risk, and preserve sufficient evidence to investigate or roll back the resulting software change
Allow generated patches to bypass review if the developer squashes the commit so the final history is simpler
explanation: AI assistance does not remove normal software-change accountability. The organization should retain useful provenance, apply risk-based review and testing, and preserve evidence so generated or edited changes can be understood, approved, investigated, and rolled back.
distractor_rationales: Functional tests alone may miss security defects, risky dependencies, authorization changes, or malicious/incorrect generated behavior.
A categorical ban is not the only risk treatment; controlled use can preserve accountability and assurance when appropriate.

AI assistance does not remove normal software-change accountability. The organization should retain useful provenance, apply risk-based review and testing, and preserve evidence so generated or edited changes can be understood, approved, investigated, and rolled back.
Squashing can simplify history but should not erase the evidence needed for review, risk decisions, and accountability.
